To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the impact of delay on predictor performance is not negligible, that the caching and overriding approaches do not work as well as the cascading lookahead approach, that a cascading lookahead branch predictor with 2K entries can achieve 95% of the accuracy of a 16K entry predictor in a single cycle, and that the cascading lookahead branch prediction approach is a good candidate for future branch prediction structures.

(1) the caching scheme provides the best accuracy and delay, (2) the overriding approach is the best for delay, but accuracy is worse, and (3) the lookahead scheme provides the worst accuracy and delay.

(1) a caching approach is not a practical method for reducing delay, (2) the overriding scheme is the best method for reducing delay and is also the most effective method for improving the accuracy of a branch predictor, and (3) the cascading approach is an effective method for reducing delay in a predictor and also improves the accuracy of the predictor.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of delay on branch prediction and the design of predictors that can accommodate delay.
the design of predictors that are both accurate and low in delay.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the cascading approach is the most effective way to deal with the delay problem, and the overriding approach is the least effective.
the cascading lookahead scheme, while requiring the most area, is the best scheme in terms of overall performance.
delay has a significant impact on the performance of branch predictors, and this impact must be considered in the design of future predictors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the impact of delay on branch prediction can be minimized by using a small branch predictor that is accessed in parallel with a larger predictor.
the cascading lookahead predictor provides the best combination of accuracy, predictability, and delay.
, in general, a predictor should be designed for a given delay budget, and that the design should be based on the delay budget, not just the accuracy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the delay of a branch predictor is a significant factor in its design.
a predictor must be designed to be delay-aware, and that a delay-aware predictor can outperform a delay-oblivious one even when the latter has better accuracy.
delay is an important factor in branch predictor design and that the design of branch predictor structures must consider the tradeoffs between delay, accuracy, and area.
